post.summary: Import an exported offline data package
post.description: Imports a zip written by a native device that could not sync, on behalf of the signed-in member. The whole package is validated and every inspection in it is authorized for the caller before anything is written, so a package that names one inspection the caller may not edit changes nothing. Importing the same package again is safe and reports its queued writes as skipped. Requires a Content-Length header.

applied.description: Queued writes executed by this import

skipped.description: Queued writes that had already been applied

status.description: HTTP status the target route refused it with, or 424 when it was not attempted because of reason

reason.description: Present when the write was not attempted: blocked_by_failed_update means an earlier queued update to the same inspection was refused, and completing the inspection without it would finish work the device never delivered. Later versions may add values; a client treats an unknown reason as "not attempted" and keeps the entry

failed.description: Queued writes the server refused. The results and photos in the package were still imported; these entries need attention on the device.

unchanged.description: Inspections whose results were already up to date

details.description: Optional structured context for the error, such as per-field validation failures.

error.description: Error detail; present only when the request failed.

meta.description: Optional response metadata, such as pagination information.

400.description: The package is malformed, names something outside its manifest, or holds an entry whose bytes do not match the size its directory declares

403.description: The package belongs to another workspace, or the caller cannot edit one of its inspections

409.description: PACKAGE_INSPECTION_DELETED: the package would create an inspection that an earlier import created and that has since been deleted; nothing was written. Also a CONFLICT whose details.reason is idempotency_in_flight: a queued write is being run by another request right now, so the import stopped and should be retried exactly as for a 5xx; writes already applied are skipped on the retry

413.description: PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE or BAD_REQUEST: the package exceeds the byte limit; details.limits names the limits

422.description: PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE: the package has more inspections, queued writes, photos or entries than this server imports at once; nothing was written. details names the limit and details.limits the sizes to split to. PACKAGE_EXPIRED: the package was exported more than details.maxAgeDays days ago; nothing was written. PACKAGE_FROM_THE_FUTURE: the package says it was exported more than details.maxFutureSkewDays day ahead of the server clock; nothing was written

post.summary: Check which local inspections the server still shows this member
post.description: Takes the inspection ids a native device holds and returns the ones that still exist in the signed-in company and that this member may see, in request order. An id that is missing from the answer was deleted, never existed, or is not visible to this member; the response does not say which, so a restricted member learns nothing about inspections outside their assignments. The device compares the answer with its local copies when it is back online. A failure is an error status and never an empty list. Read-only, though it is a POST so the ids travel in the body.

ids.description: Inspection ids the device holds locally. Between 1 and the server limit (300 by default; the limit is returned in details.limits.ids when exceeded). Each id is 1 to 64 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore and hyphen; a request that breaks any of these is refused whole with 422.

200.description: The requested ids that are visible to the caller

visible.description: The requested ids that exist in the signed-in company and that this member can see, in request order and without repeats. An id that was deleted, never existed, belongs to another company or is not assigned to this member is simply absent; the response never says which.

error.description: Error detail; present only when the request failed.

meta.description: Optional response metadata, such as pagination information.

401.description: The request does not carry a native session

422.description: The list is empty, longer than the server limit (details.limits.ids names it), or holds an id that is not 1 to 64 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore or hyphen; nothing was looked up

post.description: Publish an inspection report: sets reportStatus to published and returns the report URL. Fires the workspace's report.published automation rules (report.amended when the report was published before), so any client or agent notification is decided by those rules, not by this request; a first publish close to a sibling report's delivery may be coalesced into that notification. Also applies the automatic signature if one is configured, saves a frozen version snapshot (best effort, recorded with the optional summary), writes an inspection.published audit entry, and in the background queues the Summary and Full PDFs (only when the PDF pipeline is enabled), produces the optional courtesy translation, and syncs the report link to an ISN connection if one exists (isnSync). The theme, requireSignature, requirePayment, recipients and sendAgreementCopy fields are accepted but not used. This call does not check publish readiness; read the readiness route first. post.summary: Create a unit (Building / Floor / Unit) under an inspection
post.description: Adds one node (building, floor or unit) to the inspection's unit tree and returns its id. The tree is at most three levels deep below the top, so a parent that is already at the deepest level is refused, and a name already used by a sibling under the same parent is refused; both come back as 400. The new node is sorted after its existing siblings. A parent that is not a unit of this inspection is refused with 400. The inspection id itself is not looked up first, so an unknown id simply produces a node no inspection shows. Available to owner, manager and inspector roles.

post.summary: Bulk-create units under an inspection (floors×stacks or CSV)
post.description: Creates many units at once under one parent (or at the top level) and returns their ids. Two input styles: a floors-by-stacks grid, or pasted CSV text, each expanded into labelled units. Every created node is a regular unit. Labels that collide with an existing sibling or repeat within the batch are skipped silently, so the returned ids can be fewer than requested, or empty. All rows are inserted together. Refused with 400 when the parent is not a unit of this inspection, is already at the deepest allowed level, or the input cannot be parsed. Available to owner, manager and inspector roles.

post.description: Makes a copy of a unit as a new sibling and returns the new id. The copy keeps the original's kind, type, parent and stored attributes, gets a derived copy name that avoids sibling collisions, and is sorted last among its siblings. Findings entered against the original are not copied, so the new unit starts empty. Children of the unit are not duplicated. Refused with 400 when the unit does not exist or belongs to a different inspection. Available to owner, manager and inspector roles.

post.summary: Upload inspection for current tenant
post.description: Uploads one photo file (multipart) to the inspection's photo storage and returns its storage key. This route only stores the file: it does not add the photo to any checklist item or to the media pool, so the client must record the returned key itself. itemId must be present but is not used to place the file, and targetType and customId are only validated and echoed back (customId is required when targetType is defect). Location data is stripped from the image where the image service is available. Each call stores a new file. A file over 10 MiB is refused with 413, and a file whose declared type is not image/jpeg, image/png or image/heic with 400. Responds 400 when storage is unavailable or file or itemId is missing. Available to owner, manager and inspector roles.
